title: Knowledge check: Designing JSON Response Structures

questions.prompt: In Designing JSON Response Structures, which statement best describes Resource objects?
options: Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Keep the interface predictable for its client: use clear resource boundaries, explicit request/response formats, correct status codes, validation and tests for failure cases.

Connect this syllabus point to Designing JSON Response Structures: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
questions.answer_key: Keep the interface predictable for its client: use clear resource boundaries, explicit request/response formats, correct status codes, validation and tests for failure cases.
questions.explanation: Keep the interface predictable for its client: use clear resource boundaries, explicit request/response formats, correct status codes, validation and tests for failure cases.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Designing JSON Response Structures?
options: Model API paths around resources and align method/status-code semantics with the operation. Use consistent response envelopes, versioning, CORS configuration, idempotency where appropriate, and API documentation.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
questions.answer_key: Model API paths around resources and align method/status-code semantics with the operation. Use consistent response envelopes, versioning, CORS configuration, idempotency where appropriate, and API documentation.
questions.explanation: Model API paths around resources and align method/status-code semantics with the operation. Use consistent response envelopes, versioning, CORS configuration, idempotency where appropriate, and API documentation.

questions.prompt: A change related to Designing JSON Response Structures appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
